topic: Why the history of 'scientific' racism was funded by commercial interests
subject: history

sources.title: Anthropology and Business: Influence and Interests
Fluid Drugs: Revisiting the Anthropology of Pharmaceuticals
The Coming of the Corporate Gift
Corporate practices and health: a framework and mechanisms
New formations of power, the oligarchic-corporate state, and anthropological ideological discourse

facts.claim: Pharmaceuticals are not “discovered”; they are made and remade in relation to shifting contexts.
facts.quote: We show that there is no pure (pharmaceutical) object that precedes its socialization. Pharmaceuticals are not “discovered”; they are made and remade in relation to shifting contexts.

facts.claim: Prominent academic researchers may become intellectual “suppliers” to businesses.
facts.quote: Over time, this field has attracted prominent academic researchers (as will be discussed herein), who may become intellectual “suppliers” to businesses, and thus part of the field.

facts.claim: Corporations and other commercial interests are a distal, structural, societal factor that causes disease and injury.
facts.quote: we propose a framework to systematically study corporations and other commercial interests as a distal, structural, societal factor that causes disease and injury.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: The nation-state is complicated by the emergence to dominance of state and state-like oligarchic-corporate state formations.
facts.quote: the political environment of the nation-state is complicated by the emergence to dominance of state and state-like oligarchic-corporate state formations.

facts.claim: The field of anthropology has been influenced by the domain of business for the better part of a century.
facts.quote: the expansive domain of business... has influenced the development or “making” of anthropology as a discipline and a profession for the better part of a century

facts.claim: Commercial interests and societal concerns shape the kinds of pharmaceutical effects that are actualized.
facts.quote: This literature foregrounds insights into how commercial interests and societal concerns shape the kinds of pharmaceutical effects that are actualized

research.angle: While the sources do not specifically mention 'scientific racism' or 'exploitative labor,' they show that business interests have influenced the development of anthropology and shape the production of pharmaceuticals and societal health.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that commercial interests influence anthropological development and pharmaceutical production, but it lacks specific data on the funding of early biological studies for labor exploitation.
research.caveat: None of the provided sources contain any information regarding the specific history of 'scientific' racism or the history of labor exploitation.
